title: Periodic catalytic suppression cannot bound an isolated-pulse response horizon
statement: A positive one-state stable switched kinetic family matches fixed static endpoints and periodic mean while its isolated and identically conditioned common-hold pulse contrasts tend to zero on every fixed horizon and its conditioning time diverges.

requires: only static endpoint rates and periodic average
provides: countermodel to positive pulse-effect lower bound
countermodel to finite conditioning-time upper bound
assumptions: no separately measured transient or hidden-state-rate bound supplied
same clock and duration-matched sham for the conditioned intervention
costs: acquire conditioning/recovery trajectories over justified horizons
no fitted palladium mechanism or device performance inferred
contract.units: physical time and integrated normalized production rate
contract.obstruction: Stops periodic averages from silently becoming pulse-level causal or short-memory evidence.

evidence.quote: The number of cycles needed to condition the model tends to infinity.

review.scope: Exact source-supported extraction only; any scoped substantive acceptance is a separate version-bound review overlay.
